result.instructions:
Backend services are reached in three steps: list_services to survey, describe_service to read a signature, then call_service to invoke. Arguments are positional and orgId is injected by the server — never pass it as an argument.

AUTHENTICATION
Discovery (initialize, tools/list, list_services, describe_service) needs no credentials. call_service DOES, and requires two HTTP headers on the request:
  orgid: <organization id>
  Authorization: Bearer <token>

If you do not have a token, obtain one by signing in — this is a normal HTTP call, not an MCP tool:
  POST /user/signin   (headers: orgid)   body: { "email": "...", "password": "..." }
  -> the response carries the bearer token to use above.
An API key issued from the org (api-key endpoints) works in place of a signed-in user.

Both headers are set by whoever configured this MCP connection, not by you. If call_service reports that authentication or permission is missing, say so plainly and tell the user which header is absent — do not retry, and do not attempt to sign in on their behalf with credentials you were not given.
